title: Pick 2 fixes that can improve hero section and end of page

messages.text: We still have some room of session usage (13% lefts). Investigate the 2 fixes can improve.

Picked (04:05 +07). Both run in one Simulator session by one agent (fix-scroll-engine), to stay within the budget. (1) Hero and page end: the countdown as the cause of the small whole-page layout in ~70 % of frames at rest. The countdown changes its digits about 66 times a second, and it sits in the hero area and in the end panel. Test: the same page with the countdown hidden. If the layouts go away, the fix is already built: two countdown variants (one stops the digits repainting, one moves them as 4 layers instead of 80), so only a finger check on your phone would remain. (2) Page end: the 2 extra layouts in the first frame of the panel slide-in. Test: play the slide-in twice without reloading; if the second time is clean, the cost is a one-time first setup that can be moved earlier. Results go to T-003 (hero) and T-004 (page end).
Are they the best improvement fixes ? i'd like to pick the best improvement fixes as highest priority.

Honest answer: they are the best-supported checks for the page end, but for the hero there is a stronger candidate, so I've added it at the top. Ranking (each from your phone's own recordings, OBSERVED; no times compared, as timing is deferred): HERO #1, the accent word that redraws itself stroke by stroke. Safari's source confirms this kind of drawing forces a layout on every frame, and your phone shows about 440 small layouts per 20 s from it. It may also be the cause of the background whole-page layouts. The fix is built, but it changes how the word appears during its 1.8 s entrance (a sliding wipe instead of the stroke order; the same at rest), so it needs your OK: see Proposals, PR-001. HERO #2, the countdown check that is running now. PAGE END #1, the first frame of the panel slide-in, still about 15 ms with 2 extra layouts (running now). If you accept PR-001, it goes to a finger check on your phone next.

Understood: PR-001 is rejected, and the rule is clear: a fix must look exactly the same. So for the accent word we keep the stroke-by-stroke drawing and try a version you can't tell apart: wall off the word's box so the layout each frame stays inside that small box and doesn't spread to the whole page. Pixels stay identical. First the Simulator checks whether this word is the cause of the background whole-page layouts at all; if not, it drops off the list.
I was change from reject to change request of PR-001, did you catch up them in the claude code session ?

Yes, I see it now: PR-001 is 'change request', with your idea to play the accent word like apple.com does, as pre-rendered image frames or a video. That's a good fit: the frames would be captured from the real stroke drawing, so it looks the same, and playing frames needs no layout work at all. Plan: right after the 04:20 reset, the agent that built PR-001 (de-illusion-style) researches how apple.com does it (image sequence on a canvas vs. a video, with sharpness at your phone's 3x screen, file size and the transparent background as the checks), builds it, and sends a revised PR-001 with a side-by-side for you. Until then the Simulator check tells us how much this word costs the hero.
Did you ask team for do your 2 suggestion fixes ?

Partly. Asked and running: fix-scroll-engine is on both checks. Its first Simulator run is done (results in T-003 and T-004), and its next run is starting now: hiding parts of the page to find the background layouts' trigger (hero), and activating the end panel early (page end). Not yet asked: the frame-sequence version of the accent word (PR-001). I'm holding that until the 04:20 reset to stay inside your remaining usage, because research plus building plus a side-by-side is a bigger job. I'll send it to de-illusion-style at 04:20 and post here when it starts.

Started at 04:20: the PR-001 revision (image frames or video, like apple.com) is with de-illusion-style; details in T-006. The two Simulator checks also came back, and both suspects were wrong: the hero ring (T-003) and the page-end picture loads (T-004). The hunt for the real hero cause continues, and the page-end check is now on the real iPhone.
Catch up which the fixes that we are doing ?

Fixes in progress (04:56 +07). Numbers are our own recordings (OBSERVED).

HERO (top of page)
1. Accent word draw/erase (de-illusion-style). The hand-drawn word that redraws every 3 s makes Safari re-lay-out the whole page in the background: 622 such frames vs 72 with it off (Simulator).
   a) First: fence the word off from the rest of the page (keeps the exact animation, so nothing should look different). Being built now; checked by exact screenshot match.
   b) Your PR-001 idea: play it as pre-rendered image frames / video like apple.com. Research running.
   Both go to you on the Proposals page; you decide.
2. Rotator fix (st6): landed; you picked it in the blind swipe (C-015).

PAGE END (the panel that slides in at the bottom)
3. RB fix (the slide-in's style work): landed; you picked it (C-016), with "still laggy a bit".
4. The remaining lag: the FIRST slide-in costs about 15-20 ms extra, later ones about 2 ms (iPhone and Simulator agree). fix-scroll-engine is hunting what is "first time only". Ruled out so far: pictures, fonts, style caches, scrolling, containment. Next test (queued): showing the panel's starting state invisibly once ahead of time, plus 4 other candidates.

TOOLS that make the team faster
5. Shared test lane: ON since 04:40.
6. Phone cooling by temperature (T-009): being built.
7. Your changed proposal decisions reach me (T-007, I-045): being built.
8. Robot finger on the phone (I-042): being fixed.
9. 60 frames/s headless timing check (T-008): started 04:54.
10. Larger shared lane (T-008): being measured.

PARKED until hero and page end are done: the mid-page fixes and style-recalc work.
let's pick more 2 fixes that highest improve.

Picked: the two largest slow frames we still measure on your iPhone (our own phone recordings, OBSERVED). Both sit mid-page, between the hero and the page end:
1. The platform switch (about 2600 px down): each time the section switches while you scroll, Safari re-lays-out the whole page once, 12-18 ms. Our earlier fix removed the extra layouts around it, but this big one stayed. Its cause is still unknown; ruled out: will-change.
2. The step at about 2990 px: the hero card strip turns its rendering on/off there, and one size update costs a 14-20 ms layout. Ruled out: the size value's inheritance (registering it didn't help). Next suspect: the on/off switch itself.
Both go back to fix-scene-scope, which measured them on the phone before the pause and knows the code. It starts now, with Simulator checks using the phone's own scroll pattern; the phone only once a fix is found. Same rule as always: no visible change.

Platform-switch update (one of your 2 picks). This is from the Simulator and counts page layouts only, no timing yet.
- What the fix changes: the avatar rotator was re-laying out the whole page on every tick, about 20 ms each, 8 of 8 ticks. Stacking the already-landed rotator fix (st6) on top removes all of them: 0 of 8 ticks cause a layout now.
- What's still there: the switch's own style/layout work (about 20 ms) is unchanged. That's the next piece to work on, and the phone already pointed to the option that removes it.
- Next: a Chrome check for counts and a pixel match against the original, then the phone check once you plug it back in.

Correction on the page-middle fix (fwreskip, y≈2990): the independent review says NEEDS-WORK. I told you its settled screenshots matched. That was too strong. In Chrome, if you jump instantly into the page middle from a band around y3660-3890, the first frame after the jump shows an empty placeholder where the profile cards belong. The original page shows the cards, so this isn't pixel-identical. The jump comparisons also had no same-vs-same control. Next: the fix owner builds a variant that brings the cards back in the same scroll event, before that frame, and the hero stays untouched. It will be re-checked with controls (n≥5 per arm), plus a short up-down reversal and an idle check. Nothing lands until the review passes.

fwreskip update (page middle, y≈2990). The corrected build fixes the empty-box frame. After a sudden jump, the profile cards now show in the same frame (0 failures in 18+ runs, Chrome and Simulator). One small difference remains, and it's your call later: on the FIRST jump after a page load, two image corners in the card deck differ by a tiny amount (182-603 px, at most 4 levels out of 255). That is exactly the frame the original page paints whenever the deck is drawn fresh, e.g. after a jump from further down, so it isn't new content. But it isn't byte-identical to the original in that one scenario. A same-vs-same check never shows it. Also, scrolling back up has one extra ~20 ms layout in one run (3 vs 2), and the original-vs-original check also shows 3, so I'm getting more runs before calling it. Next: the final checks, then an independent review. I'll ask you about the corner difference with the review result.

fwreskip review #2: NEEDS-WORK, but it's closer. The empty-box frame after jumps is confirmed fixed, and the code does exactly what the README says. The reviewer found I'd been told too rosy a story in places:
(1) Scrolling down a second time after scrolling back up, the fix still has one ~20 ms layout (the original has 2), not zero. In one of 3 first descents it had 3.
(2) Sitting idle in the page middle, the fix may do more work than the original (paint +23 %, from 1 run in the Simulator). That needs repeats before anyone can say.
(3) A real-finger risk: on iPhone, Safari scrolls ahead of the page's own code. A fast flick up could briefly show the cards' empty box before the fix brings them back. The original can't do that. Only a recorded finger or gesture test on the real phone can tell.
So: the Simulator repeats run now. The fix will NOT land until the phone check is done, which means after the iPhone is plugged in by USB. Your call on the corner difference waits until then too.

fwreskip (page middle): the independent recheck ACCEPTS the corrected build's data and write-up. The reviewer recomputed every number itself. The idle question is settled: no idle cost was found once the original was measured against itself.
Two questions for you. Answer whenever you like; the fix can't land before the finger test on the iPhone anyway:
(i) Chrome only: on the first jump after a page load, two image corners in the card deck are off by up to 4 levels out of 255 (182-603 px). That's the frame the original itself paints whenever the deck is drawn fresh. Accept, or must it be byte-identical in that scenario too?
(ii) Scrolling back up after going down: the fix adds about one extra ~20 ms layout right where the cards come back, in 2 of 6 runs. In exchange it removes the two ~18 ms layouts the original does every time you scroll down past the hero. Accept that trade?
Reply 'accept both', or tell me which one to keep working on.
iPhone device is connect. you can use them.

Thanks, it's in use. The fwreskip fling test (ticket G1, your item iv) has started: both warm-up flings played correctly. The counted runs need the screen recording, so please do console step C-018 (open a QuickTime recording window for the iPhone). Your two questions (i) and (ii) in #19 are still open.

Thanks for C-018. Please don't restart iTerm: that would stop me and every agent mid-run. QuickTime does the recording with its own camera permission, and our script only sends it start/stop commands, so iTerm shouldn't need the camera. The runner is checking which command asked for it, then makes a 5 s test recording. If a permission really is missing, I'll post a System Settings step here instead, with no restart.

Fling test result for the mid-page fix (fwreskip, your item iv), first block:
- The blank card area for a moment when the people section scrolls in is NOT caused by the fix: today's build shows it too.
- But the fix has a cost on a fast fling: when the people section starts drawing again mid-fling, that frame takes 65-92 ms with the fix vs 50 ms or less without it (4 of 4 valid runs; phone timestamps, OBSERVED).
So the fix doesn't land yet. Its owner is looking at making that moment cheaper or earlier; the second block waits for that. The phone moves on to the stack test now.

Precision fix to #23: the frame numbers come from the phone's own timestamps, which count in all 5 runs with the fix (not '4 of 4 valid'). In 4 of them the slow frame (65-92 ms) is the one where the people section starts drawing again; in the 5th it is 69 ms and starts 48 ms later, at the next section. Without the fix, the longest frames were 51-57 ms.

Next step for the mid-page fix (fwreskip): its owner confirms the slow frame is built in. Whenever the people section starts drawing again during a scroll, that drawing has to happen in a frame. The only way around it is to do it while nothing scrolls. So the next version (P2) restarts the section's drawing after you stop scrolling for 0.3 s in that area. A fling after a pause would then be as smooth as today. The cost would only remain for a fling straight out of a scroll with no pause. It is built and checked on the Simulator first, then tested on the iPhone after the stack test and PR-001. If P2 doesn't remove the cost, I bring you the trade: about two 18 ms layouts saved at the hero on the way down vs one slow frame on a fast fling up.
